Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 58, verses 1–4:

It is Madani.

{1} These noble verses were revealed concerning a man of the Ansar whose wife complained to Allah and argued with him before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he had declared her forbidden to himself after a long companionship and the bearing of children. He was an elderly man, so she described her condition and his to Allah and to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and she repeated this, pressing the matter and returning to it again. Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah has heard the speech of she who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your dialogue﴾; that is, your conversation with one another. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing﴾: of all voices, at all times, in all their varied needs. ﴿Seeing﴾: He sees the crawling of the black ant upon the hard rock in the dark night.

This is a report of the perfection of His hearing and His sight, and of their encompassing of matters both subtle and great. Within this is an indication that Allah [the Exalted] will remove her complaint and lift her affliction. For this reason He mentioned her ruling and the ruling of others in general terms, so He said:

{2} ﴿Those of you who divorce [by zihar] their wives, [saying that they are] their mothers — they are not their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them﴾: Zihar from a wife is that a man says to his wife: "You are to me like the back of my mother," or like the back of any other of his mahram women, or "You are to me forbidden." The customary expression among them in this formula was "the back," and for this reason Allah called it zihar (the back-comparison). He said: ﴿Those of you who divorce their wives [by zihar]﴾; that is, how can they speak this speech which they know has no reality, comparing their wives to their mothers who gave birth to them? For this reason Allah magnified its matter and condemned it, so He said: ﴿And indeed, they utter an objectionable word and falsehood﴾; that is, a shameful statement and a lie. ﴿And indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾: toward one who has committed some transgressions and then makes amends for them with sincere repentance.

{3} ﴿And those who divorce [by zihar] their wives and then take back what they said﴾: The scholars have differed concerning the meaning of "returning" (al-'awd). It has been said that its meaning is the intention to have intercourse with the woman he has compared to his mother, and that by his mere intention the expiation mentioned becomes obligatory upon him. This is supported by the fact that Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in the expiation that it must occur before touching, and that happens only by mere intention. It has also been said that its meaning is the actual act of intercourse. This is supported by the fact that Allah said: ﴿then take back what they said﴾, and what they said was indeed intercourse. On either of the two opinions, when the "returning" occurs, the expiation for this prohibition is: ﴿the freeing of a neck﴾: a believing slave, as it is restricted in the verse on killing, male or female, on condition that it be free of defects that harm work. ﴿Before they touch one another﴾; that is, the husband is obliged to refrain from having intercourse with the wife he has compared to his mother until he has made expiation by freeing a slave. ﴿That﴾: the ruling we have mentioned to you, ﴿you are admonished by﴾; that is, it explains to you its ruling together with the warning attached to it, because the meaning of admonition is mentioning the ruling together with encouragement and warning. So whoever intends to make zihar, when he remembers that he must free a slave, restrains himself from it. ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾: He will recompense every doer for his deeds.

{4} ﴿So whoever does not find﴾: a slave to free, either because he does not find one or does not find its price, ﴿then﴾ he must ﴿fast two consecutive months before they touch one another. And whoever is not able﴾: to fast, ﴿then feeding sixty needy persons﴾: either he feeds them from the staple food of his land sufficient for them, as is the view of many of the exegetes, or he feeds each needy person a mudd of wheat or half a sa' of other foodstuffs that suffice for the charity of breaking the fast, as is the view of another group. ﴿That﴾: the ruling we have explained and clarified for you, ﴿that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾: and that is by adhering to this ruling and to other rulings and acting upon them, for adherence to the rulings of Allah and acting upon them is part of faith, indeed it is the very purpose, and by it faith increases, becomes complete, and grows. ﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾: which prevent one from falling into them, so they must not be transgressed nor fallen short of. ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.﴾

In these verses there are a number of rulings:
Among them: the gentleness of Allah toward His servants and His care for them, in that He mentioned the complaint of this afflicted woman and removed it, and lifted the affliction from her, and indeed lifted the affliction through His general ruling for everyone who is tested with a similar matter.
Among them: that zihar is specific to the prohibition of a wife, because Allah said: ﴿from their wives﴾. So if one made his slave-woman forbidden, it would not be zihar; rather it is of the kind of forbidding good things such as food and drink, in which only the expiation of an oath is obligatory.
Among them: that zihar from a woman before one marries her is not valid, because she does not enter among his wives at the time of zihar, just as her divorce is not valid, whether it is made immediate or conditional.
Among them: that zihar is forbidden, because Allah called it ﴿an objectionable word and falsehood﴾.
Among them: Allah's alerting to the ruling and its wisdom, because Allah said: ﴿they are not their mothers﴾.
Among them: that it is disliked for a man to address his wife and call her by the name of his mahram women, such as saying: "O my mother, O my sister," and the like, because that resembles what is forbidden.
Among them: that the expiation is obligatory only by the "returning" (according to the two opinions mentioned above) and not by mere zihar.
Among them: that in the expiation of freeing a slave, a young or old, male or female, is sufficient, because the verse is unrestricted in this.
Among them: that it is obligatory to complete the expiation before touching if it is by freeing or fasting, as Allah restricted it; unlike the expiation of feeding, for it is permissible to have intercourse during it.
Among them: that perhaps the wisdom in the obligation of the expiation before touching is that this is more conducive to its fulfilment, for when he desires intercourse and knows that he cannot be enabled to it except after the expiation, he hastens to perform it.
Among them: that feeding sixty needy persons is necessary; so if one gathers the food of sixty needy persons and gives it to one or more than one but fewer than sixty, that is not sufficient, because Allah said: ﴿then feeding sixty needy persons﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 58, verse 5:

{5} Muhaddah (opposing) Allah and His Messenger means opposing and disobeying them, especially in grave matters, such as opposing Allah and His Messenger with disbelief and hostility toward the friends of Allah. And His saying: ﴿They will be humiliated as those before them were humiliated﴾; that is: they will be abased and disgraced, as was done to those before them, as a fitting recompense. They have no argument against Allah, for Allah's conclusive proof has been established over creation, and He has sent down clear signs and proofs that make the realities evident and clarify the purposes. Whoever follows them and acts upon them is among the guided and the successful. ﴿And for the disbelievers﴾ in them ﴿is a humiliating punishment﴾; that is, it will disgrace and abase them. Just as they were arrogant toward the signs of Allah, He will humiliate and abase them.

{6} God, exalted is He, says: {On the Day when Allah will resurrect them} — all of creation — and they will rise swiftly from their graves, and He will recompense them for their deeds and inform them of what they did, good and bad, because He knew that and wrote it in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), and He commanded the noble angels, the recording guardians (al-Hafazah), to write it down. And yet the doers had forgotten what they did, while Allah has counted all of it. {And Allah is Witness over everything}: over the apparent and the hidden, the secret thoughts and the concealed things.

{7} For this reason He informed of the vastness of His knowledge and His encompassing of what is in the heavens and the earth, both the minute and the great, and that {there is no secret conversation of three but that He is their fourth, nor of five but that He is their sixth, nor less than that nor more but that He is with them wherever they are}. The intended meaning of this "being with" is the companionship of knowledge and encompassing of what they confide and keep secret among themselves. For this reason He said: {Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things}.

Then He, exalted is He, said:

{6} God, exalted is He, says: {On the Day when Allah will resurrect them} — all of creation — and they will rise swiftly from their graves, and He will recompense them for their deeds and inform them of what they did, good and bad, because He knew that and wrote it in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), and He commanded the noble angels, the recording guardians (al-Hafazah), to write it down. And yet the doers had forgotten what they did, while Allah has counted all of it. {And Allah is Witness over everything}: over the apparent and the hidden, the secret thoughts and the concealed things.

{7} For this reason He informed of the vastness of His knowledge and His encompassing of what is in the heavens and the earth, both the minute and the great, and that {there is no secret conversation of three but that He is their fourth, nor of five but that He is their sixth, nor less than that nor more but that He is with them wherever they are}. The intended meaning of this "being with" is the companionship of knowledge and encompassing of what they confide and keep secret among themselves. For this reason He said: {Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things}.

Then He, exalted is He, said:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 58, verses 8–9:

{8–9} The najwa (secret consultation) is confidential conversation between two or more people, and it may be for good or for evil. Allah commanded the believers to hold their consultations concerning al-birr (righteousness), which is a comprehensive term for every good and act of obedience, and for upholding the right of Allah and the rights of His servants, and taqwa (God-consciousness), which here is a comprehensive term for abandoning all that is forbidden and all sins. The believer complies with this divine command, so you will not find him conversing or speaking except about what brings him closer to Allah and distances him from His displeasure. The wicked (al-fajir) is careless about the command of Allah and converses about sin, transgression, and disobedience to the Messenger, as the hypocrites did; this was their habit and their condition with the Messenger ﷺ. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾; that is, they behave discourteously in their greeting to you. ﴿And they say within themselves﴾; that is, they conceal within themselves what the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed has mentioned about them, namely their saying: ﴿Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?﴾ The meaning of this is that they are careless about it, and they take the delay of punishment upon them as evidence that what they say is not objectionable. Allah the Exalted, explaining that He gives respite but does not neglect, said: ﴿Hell will be sufficient for them; they will burn therein, and wretched is the destination﴾; that is, Hell, which combines every punishment and wretchedness, is enough for them. It will surround them and they will be tormented by it; wretched is the destination. Those mentioned here are either some of the hypocrites, who display faith and address the Messenger ﷺ with this greeting, which gives the impression that they intended good by it, while they are liars in that; or they are some of the People of the Book who, when they greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, would say: "As-sam 'alayka ya Muhammad" (death be upon you, O Muhammad), meaning: death.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 58, verse 11:

{11} This is a courtesy (adab) from Allah to His servants [the believers] when they gather in one of their assemblies, and some of them, or some of those who arrive [at them], need room to be made for them in the assembly. For it is part of good manners that they make room for them, in order to achieve this purpose, and this does not harm the one who makes room in any way, so his brother obtains his aim without any harm reaching him. And the recompense is of the same kind as the deed: whoever makes room, Allah makes room for him, and whoever widens (the space) for his brother, Allah widens (His mercy) for him. {And when it is said, "Rise up"}; that is: rise and withdraw from your gatherings because of a need that arises, {then rise up}; that is: hasten to stand up to achieve that benefit. For standing up for such matters is part of knowledge and faith, and Allah, exalted is He, raises those who have knowledge and faith to (higher) ranks according to what Allah has specially granted them of knowledge and faith. {And Allah is Acquainted with what you do}: He will recompense every doer for his deed; if it is good, then (the recompense is) good, and if it is evil, then (the recompense is) evil. And in this verse is the virtue of knowledge, and that its adornment and its fruit is to be courteous with its manners and to act in accordance with its requirements.

{12} Allah commands the believers to give charity before privately consulting His Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), as a means of disciplining and educating them and of honouring the Messenger (ﷺ). This honouring is better for the believers and purer for them, meaning that by it their good and their reward increase, and they attain purity from the defilements, one of which is neglecting to respect the Messenger (ﷺ) and to observe proper manners with him through excessive private consultation that yields no fruit. When he commanded giving charity before private consultation with him, this became a criterion for those who were eager for knowledge and goodness: one who is eager for them does not mind giving charity, whereas one who has no eagerness or desire for goodness, and whose only aim is mere abundance of speech, refrains from it, and thereby refrains from what burdens the Messenger. This applies to one who has the means to give charity. As for one who does not find charity, Allah has not made the matter difficult for him. Rather, He pardoned him, forgave him, and permitted him to consult privately without giving a charity he is unable to afford.

{13} Then, when [Blessed and Exalted is He] saw the believers' concern and the hardship that charity posed for them at every private consultation, He eased the matter for them and did not hold them accountable for not giving charity before consultation. The honouring and respect due to the Messenger remained in their state, unabrogated (*naskh*, abrogation, the cancellation of a ruling by a later one). This ruling was a means to an end and not sought for its own sake. What is intended is good manners with the Messenger and honouring him. Allah then commanded them to perform the great obligations that are sought for their own sake, saying ﴿So when you do not do [it]﴾, meaning: giving charity did not come easily to you. This does not suffice, since it is not a condition of a command that it be easy for the servant. For this reason He qualified it by saying ﴿and Allah has turned to you [in forgiveness]﴾, meaning: He pardoned you for that. ﴿So establish the prayer﴾ (*salah*, the ritual prayer) with its pillars, conditions, all its limits and its requirements, ﴿and give zakat﴾ (the obligatory almsgiving) which is due on your wealth to those entitled to it.

These two acts of worship are the foundation of the physical and financial acts of worship. Whoever performs them in the manner prescribed by the Law has fulfilled the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants. For this reason He said after them, ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger﴾. This is the most comprehensive of commands, including obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger by carrying out their commands, avoiding their prohibitions, affirming what they have reported, and keeping within the limits of the Law. What matters in all of this is sincerity and excellence. Therefore He said, ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾. He, exalted is He, knows their deeds and the manner in which they proceeded, and He will reward them according to His knowledge of what is in their hearts.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 58, verses 14–19:

{14–15} He, exalted is He, informs of the abominable state of the hypocrites (munafiqun), who take as allies the disbelievers from among the Jews, the Christians and others, those upon whom Allah is angry and who have received the fullest share of Allah's curse. And they are neither of the believers nor of the disbelievers: ﴿wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those﴾. So they are not believers outwardly and inwardly, because their inner selves are with the disbelievers, nor are they with the disbelievers outwardly and inwardly, because their outward selves are with the believers. This is their description with which Allah has characterised them, while they swear to the opposite of it, which is falsehood. They swear that they are believers, while in fact they are not believers. So the recompense of these treacherous, wicked, lying people is that Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment whose extent cannot be measured and whose nature cannot be known; ﴿indeed, evil is what they used to do﴾, in that they did what angers Allah and necessitates for them punishment and curse.

{16} ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾; that is, a protection and a cover by which they guard themselves from the blame of Allah, His Messenger and the believers. Because of that, they have averted themselves and others from the way of Allah, which is the path that whoever travels it leads him to the Gardens of Bliss, and whoever turns away from it has nothing but the path that leads to Hellfire. ﴿So for them is a humiliating punishment﴾, because they were arrogant toward faith in Allah and submission to His verses; He humiliates them with the everlasting punishment, which will not be lightened for them for an hour, and they will not be given respite.

{17} ﴿Their wealth and their children will never avail them against Allah at all﴾; that is, they will not repel from them any of the punishment, nor will they obtain for them any portion of reward. ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire﴾: those who are constant in it, who will not leave it, and ﴿they will abide therein eternally﴾.

{18} Whoever lives upon something dies upon it. Just as the hypocrites in this world deceive the believers and swear to them that they are believers, so when the Day of Resurrection comes and Allah resurrects them all, they will swear to Allah as they swore to the believers, and in this oath they will suppose ﴿that they are upon something﴾, because their disbelief, hypocrisy and false beliefs kept taking root in their minds little by little, until they deceived them and they thought they were upon something of worth, on which reward is based, while in that they are liars. It is well known that lies do not pass before the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.

{19} This is what befell them from the domination of Satan, who has taken hold of them, adorned for them their deeds, and caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah. He is the clear enemy who desires for them nothing but evil; he only calls his party so that they may be among the companions of the blaze. ﴿Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers﴾: those who lost their religion, their worldly life, themselves and their families.

{19} This is what befell them from the domination of Satan, who has taken hold of them, adorned for them their deeds, and caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah. He is the clear enemy who desires for them nothing but evil; he only calls his party so that they may be among the companions of the blaze. ﴿Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers﴾: those who lost their religion, their worldly life, themselves and their families.

This is a promise and a warning. The warning is for those who oppose Allah and His Messenger through disbelief and disobedience: they are forsaken and humiliated, with no good end and no banner that will be victorious. The promise is for those who believe in Him and in His messengers and follow what the messengers brought, so that they become of the party of Allah, the successful: for them is conquest, victory and triumph in this world and in the Hereafter. This is a promise that will not be broken or changed, for it comes from the Truthful, the Strong, the Mighty, whom nothing that He wills can frustrate.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 58, verse 22:

{22} He, exalted is He, says: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾ — that is, this and that cannot coexist. A servant is not truly a believer in Allah and the Last Day unless he acts in accordance with what his faith requires and entails: loving those who uphold faith and allying with them, and hating and opposing those who do not uphold it, even if they are the closest of people to him. This is faith in its reality, whose fruit and purpose are realized. The people of this description are those for whom Allah ﴿has written faith into their hearts﴾ — that is, has inscribed it, established it, and planted it in such a way that it does not waver, and doubts and misgivings do not affect it. They are the ones whom Allah has strengthened ﴿with a spirit from Him﴾ — that is, with His revelation, His aid, His divine support, and His lordly favor. They are the ones who will have a good life in this abode, and for them are gardens of bliss in the abode of permanence, in which is everything the souls desire, that which delights the eyes and is chosen. For them is the best and greatest of blessings, which is that Allah causes His good pleasure to descend upon them, so He never becomes angry with them ever, and they are pleased with their Lord for what He gives them of various kinds of honors, abundant rewards, generous gifts, and elevated ranks, such that they see nothing beyond what their Master has given them as an end, nor beyond it any limit. As for the one who claims that he believes in Allah and the Last Day, yet at the same time is a friend to the enemies of Allah and loves those who have cast faith behind their backs, this is a claimed faith with no reality to it, for every matter requires proof that confirms it; mere assertion benefits nothing and its claimant is not believed. And praise be to Allah.
